# Before PR #207 (merged 2026-09-16), envBoolOr treated only the literal "true" as true, so KNOMIT_GIT_SERVE=1 set git serving to FALSE; since #207 the four bool env overrides parse with strconv.ParseBool after trimming and any other non-empty value refuses to boot naming the variable

History: on every release up to dev 3df17f54, `envBoolOr(key, target)` in internal/config/config.go did `*target = v == "true"` for any non-empty value. Git.Serve defaults to TRUE in config.Defaults, so exporting KNOMIT_GIT_SERVE=1 (or yes, on, TRUE) turned serving OFF: /git was never mounted, requests fell through to the SPA catch-all, and `git clone` reported a redirect to the site root. Observed 2026-09-15 on a live deployment while accepting PR #205. Diagnostic that still holds: the startup "knomit ready" log line carries git_remote=... only when serving is on, and "git handler enabled at /git" is logged at INFO.

Current behaviour (PR #207, dev 6f0fcc53): envBoolOr returns an error and Load propagates it, for all four bool overrides — KNOMIT_LLM_CACHE, KNOMIT_LLM_BATCH, KNOMIT_GIT_SERVE, KNOMIT_READ_ONLY. Value is TrimSpace'd; empty or whitespace-only leaves the default; strconv.ParseBool spellings (1, t, T, TRUE, true, True, 0, f, F, FALSE, false, False) apply; anything else (yes, no, on, off, 2, junk) fails boot with an error naming the variable and quoting the value. Behaviour change for deployments: a value like KNOMIT_READ_ONLY=yes booted before (silently as false) and refuses to boot now. Each call site propagating is pinned by its own test; the =1 regression is pinned end to end.

Still true: to enable serving, omit the variable (default on) or use any accepted true spelling; in knomit.toml (next to the binary, else <home>/knomit.toml) it is `[git] serve = true`. Env is applied AFTER the file, so an env value still wins over the file.

Residual asymmetry: trimming is bool-only. KNOMIT_GIT_SERVE=" true " works while KNOMIT_GIT_NETWORK_TIMEOUT=" 30s " still fails to boot; envIntOr/envFloatOr/envDurationOr do not trim. Recorded as a follow-up.

Misreadings: pre-#207, "=1 is ignored" was wrong — it was APPLIED as false. Post-#207, "on/off are accepted" is wrong — they refuse to boot, and the error lists the accepted spellings.
